messages:
Rachel: Quick sync — we need a lightweight consent/approval surface in Console for scoped tokens and service-account grants. Enterprise tenants want admin approval for any role grant that opens routes beyond their default scope. Proposal: show a one-click consent modal when a scoped-token is created that requires an admin to approve; persist audit + telemetry. Thoughts?
Sam: agree we need it. question: should Console call the policy evaluation API to figure out whether a grant needs approval, or should we have a deterministic client-side rule?
Lia: prefer server-side check via /v1/policy/eval so we centralize logic. client-side heuristics get out of sync. also easier for webhook alerts.
Drew: +1 on /v1/policy/eval. but that adds latency during token create. might want an async workflow: create token in pending state, kick approval job, show spinner.
Ana: UX thought — modal should show a diff of entitlements (compact list), and an explicit "Request approval" CTA that triggers a 2FA prompt for the approver. also show cost/route impact: e.g., model routing to dedicated vs hosted.
Rachel: good. Sam — what's the API shape you'd expect? maybe POST /admin/grants with body and it returns {status: pending|approved, reason}?
Sam: something like: ```json
POST /v1/admin/grants 
{
  "principal": "svc-chatbot-123",
  "requested_scopes": ["route:openai-compat", "embed:vector-search"],
  "requester": "mike@example.com"
}
```
Response: ```json
{ "grant_id": "g_abc123", "status": "pending", "requires_approval": true }
```
Then an approver calls POST /v1/admin/grants/g_abc123/approve with audit payload.
Lia: and we should capture telemetry events: consent.requested, consent.approved, consent.denied, consent.expired. include org_id, approver_id, grant_delta, routing_impact (e.g., routes_added).
eng-security-bot: reminder: store audit entry in immutabledb and emit to org-audit-log with envelope sig. Also record request reason for compliance.
Drew: rollout plan: behind feature-flag "consent_ui_v1". Canary to 5-10% of orgs, then 25% with extra logging. We should not block service-account creation in early canary — mark pending but allow fallback for emergency via "auto-approve" policy for some admin roles.
Ana: UX copy: "This token requests access to additional routes and resources. An org admin must approve before it can be used in production." then secondary link to "Why this is required". Keep it short.
Rachel: Implementation tasks: 1) policy/eval flag to indicate requires_confirmation, 2) grants API + Approve/Reject endpoints, 3) Console modal + audit UI entry, 4) telemetry events and dashboard tile for consent latency/failure rates. Who picks up which?
Sam: I can do API (1 & 2). Lia will wire policy/eval changes. Drew will handle backend audit storage and rollout flags. Ana will design modal and copy. Rachel will coordinate QA and feature-flag rollout.
Ana: I'll mock up screens by EOD tomorrow and add small a11y checklist.
Lia: note: need to consider quota evaluation — approved grants might increase token consumption on dedicated pools; we should surface quota warning.
Rachel: good catch. add quota-warning line to modal and telemetry. Ok team — let's treat this as high priority for enterprise FY24 Q2. :thumbsup:
eng-security-bot: deploy-bot triggered: feature-flag created: consent_ui_v1 (owner: eng-platform).
